- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above prior peak.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) and price is falling, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in early 30d horizon — if price is trending sharply, forecast should lag 1–2 days to align with sentiment-driven correction.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture volatility; increase forecast variance by ±1–2% to reflect sentiment uncertainty.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome is below 60% of 30d mean, model is overconfident; apply downward bias of 2–5% unless sentiment strongly supports upside.
